instructions: Take the yogurt out of the fridge first. Thinly slice the 2 onions and set aside one onion's worth, about 1 cup, in a bowl for the pakoras. Finely chop 1 tbsp of the ginger and the 4 garlic cloves. Chop 1/4 cup of the cilantro for the pakoras and 2 tbsp for the kadhi. Thinly slice the green chili and put it in a small bowl for the table.

In a large bowl, whisk 1/2 cup of the gram flour into 1 1/2 cups yogurt until smooth. Whisk in 1/2 tsp of the turmeric, 1/2 tsp of the chili powder and the 1 tsp ground coriander until there are no lumps, then whisk in 6 cups water.

Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a large, deep pot over medium high. Add the 1/2 tsp fenugreek seeds and 1/2 tsp of the cumin seeds. When they sizzle and turn a shade darker, after about 20 seconds, stir in the 1/4 tsp asafoetida.
Add the kadhi onion and cook for 2 minutes, until it starts to soften. Add the ginger and garlic and cook for about 1 minute, until they just start to color.
Pour in the yogurt mixture and keep stirring over medium high until it comes to a boil, 8 to 10 minutes. Don't stop stirring until it boils, or the yogurt can split.

Turn the heat to medium low and simmer for 30 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes or so, until it's thickened and tastes nutty rather than floury. After the first 15 minutes, stir in 1 1/4 tsp of the salt.

Meanwhile, make the pakora batter. Mix the pakora onion with the remaining 1 cup gram flour, the 1/4 cup cilantro, the last 1/4 tsp turmeric, 1/4 tsp of the chili powder, the 1/2 tsp coriander seeds, 1/4 tsp of the ajwain and the last 1/2 tsp salt. Add about 1/3 cup water a little at a time, mixing with your hand, until it's a thick batter that clings to the onions. Mix in the 1/8 tsp baking soda.

Heat the rest of the oil, about 1 3/4 cups, in a deep skillet or small heavy pot over medium. You're aiming for about 350°F, so if you have a thermometer, check it. No thermometer? Drop in a little batter. It should sizzle and float up within a few seconds.

Drop in walnut sized spoonfuls of batter, 6 or 7 at a time. Fry for 2 to 3 minutes, until golden brown underneath. Flip them and cook the other side for 2 to 3 minutes. If they brown much faster than that, turn the heat down a little. Lift them onto paper towels and fry the rest the same way.

When the kadhi has had its 30 minutes, it should coat the back of a spoon and still pour easily. If it's thicker than that, stir in a splash of hot water. Stir in the 2 tbsp cilantro, add the pakoras and simmer for 2 minutes. Take the pot off the heat.

Melt 1 1/2 tbsp ghee in a small pan over medium. Add the remaining 1/4 tsp cumin seeds, the last 1/4 tsp ajwain and the 2 dried red chilies. When the seeds crackle, take the pan off the heat, stir in the last 1/2 tsp chili powder and pour it straight over the kadhi.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve with steamed rice, with the sliced green chili on the side.
method_notes: All three whisk gram flour into yogurt and plenty of water, temper fenugreek and cumin seeds with asafoetida, then stir the kadhi constantly until it boils so it doesn't split and simmer it 20 to 30 minutes until the raw flour taste is gone. The onion pakoras are a thick gram flour batter with ajwain and a pinch of baking soda, fried while the kadhi cooks, and everyone finishes with a ghee tadka of cumin, dried red chilies and Kashmiri chili. Cook with Manali uses more water and a 30 minute simmer and adds the salt partway through; Swasthi's also adds ginger and garlic and a little garam masala, and suggests adding the pakoras at serving if you like them crisp; Piping Pot Curry adds mustard seeds and curry leaves to the first tempering. This one follows Manali's ratios and puts the fresh green chili on the side.
